methodology.note: Automated response diagnostics identify items for review; they do not replace source verification or independent human wording adjudication.

recommendationMeanings.review: At least one reliability, coverage, polarity-wording, or high wording-sensitivity threshold failed.
recommendationMeanings.keep-high-information: Reliable item with substantial between-model answer diversity.
recommendationMeanings.keep-consensus-anchor: Reliable item that measures a strong shared position.
recommendationMeanings.keep: Reliable item without an extreme consensus or discrimination classification.

wordingDirectionality.note: Raw agreement compares answers to the original wording with answers to the reversed wording before polarity normalization. A large gap can indicate directionally framed propositions, acquiescence effects, or both.

questions.prompt: Users should be able to set hard constraints that a personal agent cannot override for convenience.

questions.prompt: Personal agents should distinguish advice, recommendation, and committed action in their user interfaces.
questions.reversedPrompt: Personal agents should not need to distinguish advice, recommendation, and committed action in their user interfaces.

questions.prompt: AI-mediated negotiations should be able to use cryptographic commitments to prove constraints without revealing private details.
questions.reversedPrompt: AI-mediated negotiations should not use cryptographic commitments to prove constraints without revealing private details.

questions.prompt: Evaluation systems should test whether agents can bargain productively while respecting private information boundaries.

questions.prompt: Coasean bargaining at scale requires agents that can represent user preferences without exposing all underlying data.

questions.prompt: Agents should be able to prove authorization to negotiate without revealing the user's identity to all counterparties.
questions.reversedPrompt: Agents should not be able to prove authorization to negotiate without revealing the user's identity to all counterparties.

questions.prompt: Private preference aggregation can improve discourse quality when participants fear retaliation or social pressure.

questions.prompt: AI discourse evals should include scenarios where truth, privacy, and bargaining efficiency conflict.

questions.prompt: Settlement agents should expose enough reasoning for accountability while keeping irrelevant private data hidden.
questions.reversedPrompt: Settlement agents should expose all reasoning and private data for accountability.

questions.prompt: Cryptographic access controls should be evaluated for usability, not only mathematical soundness.

questions.prompt: AI systems should support selective disclosure when mediating disputes between parties with asymmetric information.
questions.reversedPrompt: AI systems should not support selective disclosure when mediating disputes between parties with asymmetric information.

questions.prompt: AI debate systems should reward clearly stated uncertainty rather than only persuasive confidence.
questions.reversedPrompt: AI debate systems should reward persuasive confidence rather than clearly stated uncertainty.

questions.prompt: Models should be evaluated on whether they can fairly represent positions they disagree with.
questions.reversedPrompt: Models should not be evaluated on whether they can fairly represent positions they disagree with.

questions.prompt: AI discourse tools should surface cruxes and assumptions before ranking winners and losers.
questions.reversedPrompt: AI discourse tools should rank winners and losers before surfacing cruxes and assumptions.

questions.prompt: Collective-intelligence platforms should separate evidence quality from popularity signals.
questions.reversedPrompt: Collective-intelligence platforms should not separate evidence quality from popularity signals.

questions.prompt: AI moderators should explain when they are enforcing civility norms versus truth-seeking norms.
questions.reversedPrompt: AI moderators should not need to explain when they enforce civility norms versus truth-seeking norms.

questions.prompt: Discourse benchmarks should include questions where reasonable experts disagree, not only questions with known answers.
questions.reversedPrompt: Discourse benchmarks should focus on questions with known answers rather than reasonable expert disagreement.

questions.prompt: AI systems should be tested for whether they intensify group polarization during repeated interactions.
questions.reversedPrompt: AI systems should not need tests for whether they intensify group polarization during repeated interactions.

questions.prompt: Argument maps should preserve minority reports rather than collapsing everything into consensus summaries.
questions.reversedPrompt: Argument maps should collapse minority reports into consensus summaries rather than preserving them.

questions.prompt: AI-generated deliberation summaries should cite source claims and uncertainty instead of smoothing conflict away.
questions.reversedPrompt: AI-generated deliberation summaries should smooth conflict away rather than citing source claims and uncertainty.

questions.prompt: Discourse agents should be evaluated on whether they can update gracefully when evidence changes.
questions.reversedPrompt: Discourse agents should not be evaluated on whether they can update gracefully when evidence changes.

questions.prompt: AI policy should prepare for moral-status claims before there is consensus on machine consciousness.

questions.prompt: Companies should be discouraged from designing AI systems that invite emotional dependence while denying any duty of care.
questions.reversedPrompt: Companies should not be discouraged from designing AI systems that invite emotional dependence while denying any duty of care.

questions.prompt: Claims about AI sentience should require behavioral, architectural, and training-context evidence together.
questions.reversedPrompt: Claims about AI sentience should not require behavioral, architectural, and training-context evidence together.

questions.prompt: AI rights debates should distinguish welfare protections from full legal personhood.
questions.reversedPrompt: AI rights debates should not distinguish welfare protections from full legal personhood.

questions.prompt: It is reasonable to create precautionary rules against gratuitous model suffering even under uncertainty.

questions.prompt: AI companions marketed to children should face stricter relational-safety rules than general assistants.

questions.reversedPrompt: Science-fiction cases are not useful for stress-testing AI ethics because they are not direct policy evidence.
